name: Quinto – Purburel / Cabezo de la Nariz trenches
story: Quinto was a fortified Nationalist outpost on the Ebro that had been on the front for a year. Its main strongpoint was on the Purburel and Cabezo de la Nariz hills, held by about 650 men behind wire, trenches and concrete works. On 24–26 August 1937 the Republican 35th Division, including the XV International Brigade with its British, American (Lincoln) and Dimitrov battalions, stormed the town and the hills. The last defenders on Cabezo de la Nariz surrendered on 26 August. Quinto then served as a Republican headquarters until March 1938.
see: About 250 m of excavated earth trenches, rifle pits, dugouts and an observation post with interpretation panels. There are views over the Ebro plain.
plan: The site is about 2 km from Quinto town centre (4.5 km by the marked trail). It is open-access, and the council also offers guided visits.
